package_info.package_manager: N/A (Java web server, distributed as binaries/source)
package_info.why_malicious: Multiple vulnerabilities allow attackers to bypass security constraints, cause denial of service, and achieve remote code execution. These flaws can be exploited to gain unauthorized access, disrupt service, or fully compromise the server.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Allows unauthorized access to protected resources by exploiting the order of endpoint access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Security constraints are expected to protect all sub-resources, but a specific access order bypasses them.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior: All /account/* endpoints require authentication. Actual: /account/withdrawal can be accessed without authentication if accessed first.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; security constraints should always be enforced.
key_indicators: Access to protected endpoint without authentication

execution_context.trigger: HTTP/2 request with large header field

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Causes Tomcat to enter an infinite loop, resulting in denial of service.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: A malformed or oversized header should be rejected, not cause infinite processing.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal: Server returns error for malformed/oversized headers. Actual: Server hangs, consuming resources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; legitimate clients do not send headers designed to trigger infinite loops.
key_indicators: Infinite loop on malformed HTTP/2 headers

execution_context.trigger: HTTP request to CGI servlet with crafted parameters (Windows only)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Injects arbitrary commands into the CGI process, allowing remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: User input is not properly sanitized, allowing command injection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal: Parameters are passed safely to scripts. Actual: Parameters are executed as commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use: Passing safe parameters to scripts. Illegitimate: Injecting shell commands.
key_indicators: Unescaped user input in command line
Ability to execute arbitrary OS commands

execution_context.trigger: Deserialization of crafted JSF view state

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: JexBoss exploit tool sends crafted view state to trigger code execution.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Allows attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server by exploiting unsafe deserialization.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deserialization of untrusted data is a well-known vector for RCE.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal: View state is signed and validated. Actual: Attacker can inject code via view state.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate: Restoring UI state. Illegitimate: Executing attacker-supplied code.
key_indicators: Remote code execution via crafted view state

attack_chain.action: Attacker identifies vulnerable endpoint or configuration (e.g., /account/withdrawal, CGI servlet, JSF view state).
Attacker sends crafted HTTP request to exploit the vulnerability (bypass, DoS, or RCE).
attack_chain.leads_to: Gains unauthorized access, causes denial of service, or achieves remote code execution.

attack_chain.action: If RCE is achieved, attacker can execute arbitrary commands or open a shell on the server.

behavioral_signatures: Access to protected endpoints without authentication
HTTP/2 requests with abnormally large headers causing server hangs
Unusual parameters in CGI requests (especially on Windows)
Deserialization of untrusted JSF view state data
file_indicators: web.xml or servlet annotations with misconfigured security constraints
Presence of CGI servlet enabled in Tomcat
JSF applications with unsigned or weakly protected view state
network_indicators: Repeated access attempts to /account/withdrawal or similar endpoints
HTTP/2 requests with very large headers
Unusual POST data to JSF endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized access to protected endpoints, HTTP/2 requests with oversized headers, and suspicious parameters in CGI or JSF requests. Use web application firewalls (WAFs) to block known exploit patterns. Regularly audit server configurations for insecure settings (e.g., enabled CGI servlet, weak JSF view state protection). Enable logging and alerting for authentication bypasses, server hangs, and command execution attempts.
